utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Riedlmayer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Your evidence will continue now, subject to the usual rule that the solemn declaration which you took at the beginning to tell the truth continues to apply to that evidence today. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. When we stopped yesterday, I said I had no more questions for the witness, but there had been a couple matters that have come up in connection with some satellite photos and regarding whether or not there were additional text pages in his database concerning a couple of the mosques in Vushtrri that we showed photos for but we did not show the related pages, and also some issues about the so-called White Book regarding Serbian allegations about NATO damage to Serbian monuments which he spoke to. And I would like to ask him a few questions about some of those matters, if I may, to confirm whether or not the satellite photos we do have to confirm whether they are the ones he's talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes. Please carry on, then.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And regarding the White Book, a couple of questions as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Mr. Riedlmayer, yesterday, a couple of times, you mentioned satellite photos and they're referenced in your database as part of your source for the information regarding either the pre-existence of a particular site or the damage or both.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I would like the registry officer to bring up P98 for us, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: This regards Bela Crkva. You mentioned that there -- that you had seen a satellite photograph showing damage -- well, both before and after pictures concerning the mosque. I'm not sure of the quality that's in e-court, and I have a hard copy that I could ask the usher to hand you as well. Yes, I think your hard copy may be better, and I don't know if the hard copy will show up better on the ELMO than the e-court version does.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Please put the hard copy on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And while we're getting the ELMO started, Mr. Riedlmayer, do you recognise that photograph?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Is that the one you were referring to yesterday?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was. On the hard copy, at least, you can see on the left the mosque intact with a minaret and a big dome and a series of little domes to the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. If we could have you handed the pointer and then if you could point to the photograph on the ELMO and indicate where you're talking about. On the left it's described as --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the speakers please slow down and make pauses between questions and answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: "Buildings Intact, 11 March 1999." Can you tell us where the mosque is on that photograph?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The left-hand photograph, at the very centre here, is the image of the mosque; in the middle, the tall thin structure is the minaret; to the right is the large dome over the prayer hall; to the left, the small domes over the entrance.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And the right half of that exhibit is described as buildings damaged 2 April 1999, and I recall when we had the opening statement, and at the bottom of this photograph there's a notation, that this appears to be the same area but 180 degrees rotated, based on the curve of the river. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You can also orient yourself again. This time the main dome of the mosque is on the left of the building and the small domes, on the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And are you able to tell whether the minaret is still --

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The minaret doesn't appear to be there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Next I would like to show you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Riedlmayer, how did you obtain this photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was displayed on the web, on the NATO web site.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Next, could we show you on the e-court Exhibit P2455. You mentioned yesterday, when we were talking about the library and the mosque in Djakovica, that you had seen a photo, a satellite photo, showing actually that area burning and while the minaret was still intact.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I have a hard copy that may be slightly better than what's on the screen.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The screen version isn't very bad.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Let's just go with the screen version.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Let's go with the screen, then.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the centre of the image you see the mosque with the minaret to the left - it's the very thin structure - and to the left of that, the library. And the street running diagonally from top to bottom to the left of that is the street of shops that I was referring to with the individual shops on both sides of the street missing their roofs. Their interiors are vacant; they are burned out. And what's remarkable to me is that none of the buildings of the street, meaning to the left of the street, beyond the row of burnt shops, appears to be damaged in any way. You can see a large cloud of smoke rising just above the mosque. If you look at the hard copy, probably you can see more detail as to exactly where the smoke is rising from. I assume it's rising from some of the shops, but it also appears to be rising from the library building.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And where did you obtain this photo?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This photo is still available on the US Department of Defence web site.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, how do we establish the date of this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the web site it appears with the date. I believe, I'm speaking from memory, but I believe the date may be the 25th of March, so the day after the first NATO air-strikes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And is that consistent with other information you obtained about when the damage occurred in that area as far as burning of buildings versus when the minaret was toppled?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Your Honour, with respect to this mosque, with your permission, I'd like to say something concerning the question you asked me yesterday ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Remind me what the question was, Mr. Riedlmayer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The question was who was the person who informed me about the details of the destruction of the mosque.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And last night I thought about it some more. It was an October morning, seven years ago, almost exactly, and I thought about who I spoke with that morning and I am quite sure it was Mr. Boshi. He was the only person we spoke to at the mosque site, and as I recall now, he wasn't the imam of the mosque but a senior member of the congregation of the mosque.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And finally, if we could show Exhibit P2456 [Realtime transcript read in error "2445"] to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yesterday, Mr. Riedlmayer, we showed you some photos of a damaged mosque in Vushtrri. The first one we showed you was the one that was completely destroyed, and then we showed you two others from which the minaret had been toppled, but we didn't have related text pages from your database. I'd like to show you now, if you look at the screen on the first page there, we looked at a photo of the Karamanli mosque. Are these the pages from your database that relate to that mosque?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, I'm confused by this number, Mr. Hannis, because we had P2445 yesterday and it was a pre-war photo of the mosque at Celine.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That was 2445, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And that's what this one bears to be, according to the transcript. Have I got the wrong number?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I believe this one should be 2456, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's wrongly recorded, then, on the transcript. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I may have misspoken, Your Honour. And if we could just scroll down to the bottom of this page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There, you see the two photographs shown in court yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And if we could go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That's a pre-war photograph on the right?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: It's just your bibliography concerning that entry.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Does this relate to the third photograph of a mosque in Vushtrri that we looked at yesterday?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Scroll to the bottom, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And the top photo was the one that we saw yesterday?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And what is on the bottom of that?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the bottom is a second photograph of the mosque that I took.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could we go to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is a pre-war photo with the minaret intact.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And the next page. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Those are the pages from your database that related to those additional two photographs we showed yesterday?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, one other thing I wanted to ask you about concerned the so-called White Book. Do you recall what the full title of that document is?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is cited in the last section of my report, of my expert report, among the sources of allegations, and the title is indicated there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Is that "NATO Crimes in Yugoslavia"?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And it's two volumes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Divided chronologically between the 24th of March and the 24th of April, in volume 1?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I see them in front of you there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Those are the ones in which you said there were allegations of damage by NATO bombing that you checked out and they appeared to be accurate.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we tried to check every allegation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe that's all the additional questions I had.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: I have a question, just to clarify certain things. For purposes of verifications, did you refer only to the University of Harvard repository, or were you able to also check things or verify facts from other such repositories, like Topkapi in Istanbul and the British museum, or the one, the Louvre, as you call it, in France? Because these are also repositories on these areas. Topkapi would be very essential, just to check that. And the second was, when you talk about "NATO Crimes in Yugoslavia," is this a book now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is a two-volume book.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: Thanks. I'm grateful for that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And with respect to libraries, I worked for three months to gather documentation primarily from the Harvard libraries, but I also approached other libraries when materials were not available at Harvard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Ivetic, do you wish to take up the issue of objections to exhibits?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, it was brought to my attention that I indicated we would do that at the conclusion of direct. I think the prior witnesses we had similar objections to we waited until all the evidence was in. So I propose we do that so we don't take up cross-examination time with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. O'Sullivan.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, the order will be: General Lazarevic, Mr. Sainovic, General Pavkovic, General Ojdanic, Mr. Milutinovic, and General Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Riedlmayer, I'm Mihajlo Bakrac, attorney-at-law, one of the Defence counsel for General Vladimir Lazarevic. At the outset, I wish to go through your CV. And with respect to professional associations, I see that you're a member of the Society for Turkish Studies, also Historians of Islamic Art, Middle East Librarians Association, Society for Iranian Studies, Art Libraries Society of North America, Middle East Studies Association of North America, and International Association of Orientalist Librarians. Is all of this correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Apart from that, Mr. Riedlmayer, when talking about your professional experience, from the very beginning of your professional career, you worked on the Ottoman Empire and Islamic culture. Is that also correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: When we look at your publications, mostly, they all refer to the Ottoman Empire and the Islamic cultural heritage. Is that also correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most of them do. I have written about Serbian heritage as well, however.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: But, Mr. Riedlmayer, nowhere in your publications have I found anything not about the Serb heritage but about Orthodox or Catholic cultural heritage. Perhaps you may have mentioned it in passing or when discussing Bosnia, but nowhere do I see any publication dealing with that heritage.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have written on Orthodox heritage in Bosnia. If you have the most recent version of my curriculum vitae, you may see an article on Zito Mislic, the Serbian Orthodox monastery in Herzegovina. That was destroyed during the war in Bosnia. I have also an article about -- two articles that deal with the destruction of Serbian Orthodox monuments in Kosovo, both during the 1999 period and, more recently, in March of 2004.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Riedlmayer, perhaps I really do not have your latest CV, but you will agree that the two articles mentioned, compared to everything else in your eight-page CV, is not very much, because most of it refers to the Ottoman Empire and the Islamic cultural heritage. So you will agree with me, will you not, that you spent almost your entire career studying the Ottoman Empire and the Islamic cultural heritage?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no wish to dispute that; it's my academic specialty.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Riedlmayer. Yesterday, you said that you initiated a project concerning the cultural heritage in Kosovo, in June 1999. And you also told us that in June and July, you had some information about the events in Kosovo. From where did you glean this information?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In June and July, when I hadn't done my field-work in Kosovo yet, the information came primarily from published sources, as the war ended and Kosovo became accessible to international media. I also had some contact with individuals who had travelled to Kosovo and relayed their information to me via e-mail, both professionals and journalists.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you then have any contacts with people or experts from Human Rights Watch?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you read their reports from the ground?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am -- I saw their reports. My primary contact, in terms of human rights organisations, was with Physicians for Human Rights, who are mentioned in my report as one of the sources of allegations.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you also read the reports about allegations made by refugees from Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was what I just referred to. Physicians for Human Rights had an interview project during the war where they interviewed heads of households among refugees from Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: In June and July 1999, when you conceived the idea of initiating this action, did you know that an indictment had been brought against Slobodan Milosevic, who was still then the President?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was public knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Were you also aware of what the indictment contained? Did you read it?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Before you set out for the field, you first came to the OTP, in The Hague, to offer your services. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I offered my services, actually, before setting out. Asking -- simply asking the Office of the Prosecutor whether they would be interested in any data I collected. And they suggested, and strongly urged, that I visit The Hague before I go into the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Wasn't it logical, Mr. Riedlmayer, for you to first go out to the field and gather information in the shortest possible time-period, rather than visiting the OTP before setting out?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The visit to the OTP took one afternoon, on the way from Boston to Skopije and Pristina. It did not significantly delay our investigations.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And what task - if I may call it that - were you given by the OTP? What was to be the subject of your investigation in the field?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were not commissioned to do this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just a moment, Mr. Riedlmayer. That question has been answered. Now, I know you're entitled to cross-examine, but if there's a particular point on which you wish to cross-examine, Mr. Bakrac, then you should try to focus it more quickly. But the witness already explained in full his contact with the OTP, and if you have a challenge to make, then please focus on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Riedlmayer, what was your main task in the field? What task did you set for yourself on arrival in Kosovo? What did you focus on mostly in your investigations?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: We focused on -- within the limits of our capabilities, in terms of time available and sites that were accessible, to visit every site concerning which there had been an allegation of damage during or immediately after the war; and having visited, to document what we saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: To document and establish the damage that had been caused. Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: But your task was not to investigate and establish who caused the damage and how. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only in a secondary way. Our primary task was to record the damage. If there were observations to be made about the damage that could establish when and how it was inflicted, then we would record that as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: It was only you and Mr. Herscher who did the surveys.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were the only ones who did the assessments. Obviously we were assisted by photographs and other information that we collected from other sources.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you have someone in your team who understands ballistics or military matters? Did you have any military experts with you?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge of ballistics or military knowledge?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not a military expert, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: In your analysis, you determined exactly in your expertise that you assessed both the Islamic and the Serb Orthodox and the Catholic cultural heritage. I note that, regarding the Islamic heritage, you stated the exact number of mosques and other cultural property, while your report on the subject of Serb Orthodox and Catholic cultural property does not state the exact number. Why is that?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the number of pre-war mosques and pre-war churches, we had to rely on published information. In the case of the mosques, we were fortunate to find a pre-war published source. In the case of the Orthodox churches, if you read my discussion in our expert report, you will see that we discussed the problem that most of the literature does not clearly distinguish between archaeological ruins and intact churches. By the parameters of our study, we excluded archaeological sites; only dealt with buildings that had been intact before the war. The closest we could come was a publication of the Republican Institute for the Preservation of Heritage -- Preservation of Monuments of Serbia, published very shortly before the war, which listed a total of 210 Serbian Orthodox churches and monasteries that were regarded as protected monuments. I assume that that is a subset of a larger number, which includes buildings that were not considered significant enough to be granted legal protection.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And outside that list of protected monuments, did you inquire into others? Because you did so with Islamic monuments. With regard to Serbian Orthodox monuments, did you inquire into those that did not have such legal protection?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We were fortunate in that the Serbian Orthodox church, especially during the period of our survey, was very active in publicising damage to Serbian Orthodox churches in Kosovo. They published a book called "Crucified Kosovo," which appeared just as we arrived there. They also put this information up on the internet. That listed a total of 80 churches that had been damaged or destroyed in the months after the war. We visited as many as we could, and for the remainder, we either took information from the church web site and from "Crucified Kosovo," or we exchanged photographs with Father Sava Janjic. Some of our photographs subsequently appeared on the Orthodox church web site.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Riedlmayer, what I would like to know, in light of all my previous questions -- in fact, what I'm especially interested in is that in your expert report regarding Islamic monuments, you stated precisely which mosques are active, which are out of use. And we don't know any such thing regarding Serbian Orthodox temples; we don't know how many of them are in use, how many of them you have seen. Can you tell me why?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In terms of the number that we have seen, I believe that is listed in our report. In terms of the number that are in or out of use, again, there didn't happen to be a published source that gave that figure.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You did not find anywhere a single source where that number would be included?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I tried to tell you earlier, we looked at a lot of published information on Orthodox heritage in Kosovo. One of the most recent and comprehensive is a book by Gojko Subotic, "Kosovo Art of the Sacred Land," which includes many, many sites, but it does not distinguish between sites that are standing, sites which are medieval ruins, and sites which are merely mentioned in medieval charters but of which no traceable ground exists today. Since he did not provide the statistic, we did not feel it necessary to try to calculate our own.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you, Mr. Riedlmayer. If I understood your testimony yesterday well, you personally assessed 144 monuments in Kosovo before making your expert report. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you have any record, perhaps, as to how many of those buildings that you personally visited fall into the category of Islamic heritage?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it's mentioned in my report. I don't recall it off-hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness does have a hard copy. And your report, Mr. Riedlmayer, is located at tab, I believe, 1789, if that assists.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But I can give you an approximation, if you wish.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Riedlmayer, we'll not waste time on details. I'll try to assist you. Do you agree with me that you visited personally around 100 buildings of Islamic heritage?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is probably correct. In terms of Orthodox heritage, simply as an economy of time, given that so much documentation had been made available by the Serbian Orthodox church, we did not try to duplicate many of their already-documented sites but concentrated on sites for which they did not have documentation, which is how we were able to exchange information with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Riedlmayer, again, if I understood you correctly when you spoke yesterday, out of 225 damaged Islamic monuments, you visited less than half, that is, around a hundred. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. For the rest, we relied on documentation from other sources, photographs and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Therefore, you based your expert report concerning that other half on photographs. You based your assessments on photographs. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Wherever possible, we would try to confirm any information from multiple, independent sources. We included no sites for which we didn't have photographic evidence, but if there was other corroborating evidence, such as, you know, the Institute for Protection of Monuments mentioning that a site was destroyed, we would mention that in our report. But the photographs were what we primarily relied on.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Riedlmayer, I'm interested in this: Is it possible for a serious assessment of damage to be made only on the basis of photographs?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Given that our criteria were based on plainly observable visual evidence - we were not out there doing technical tests - it was possible as long as the photograph was legible and showed clearly discernible damage to say something meaningful about the damage on the basis of only the photograph. If you see a building without a roof, if you see a building covered with soot, or if you see a pile of rubble, there are certain conclusions that you can draw from that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes. Conclusions may be on the degree of damage, but you will agree with me that one cannot make any conclusions, on that basis, about the way damage was inflicted?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would disagree with that. If a building has been destroyed by a blast, it leaves a very different kind of ruin than a building which has either been burnt down or vandalised. So I think there are ways in which you can draw conclusions regarding the nature of the damage.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: When you say "explosives" or "blast," do you know that there are cruise missiles and grenades that also contain explosives; that there are rockets that set on fire the building they hit? Are you aware of that? You did say you were not a military expert, or an expert in ballistics, but you are now making an excursion into that field. So I would like to know whether you can make the distinction.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not a military expert; therefore, I cannot distinguish between different calibres of munitions used or kinds of munitions used. But, first of all, I have, in the course of my field-work, observed hundreds of buildings that have been damaged. I have also read a good deal of the technical literature; and, therefore, for example, know that a building that has been burned from the inside will have a very different look from a building that has been hit by any kind of aerial munitions. I can give you a very specific example, if you like. In many cases, in Kosovo, you saw buildings that had been burned. And if the -- if you went into the building, the entire inside of the building would be carpeted by an even layer of roof tiles, totally undisturbed. I think it is a sensible conclusion, even if you are not a military expert, that the roof simply collapsed due to a fire, rather than that something smashed through the roof. You know, I think a lot of this is simply common sense.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Precisely, Mr. Riedlmayer. So when making your assessments, you were guided by common sense. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Common sense informed by experience and research.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Riedlmayer, I'll move on to a different subject, but I have to tell you, unfortunately, I have lived through a bombardment. And I know that cruise missiles can go through a window --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It may be bring some comfort to Mr. Bakrac, but it important that we confine our questions and the evidence to that of the witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, just in case, if you have an objection, I wanted to mention that I did live through a bombardment. So you should bear that in mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It doesn't really show, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour. I hope that was sincere.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So, Mr. Riedlmayer, I'll rephrase my question. Do you know that there are rockets with a lower charge, very precise, that can fly even through a smoke pipe? That's my last question on this subject. Are you aware of this?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you, military is not my expertise.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Riedlmayer. When you were working on the ground and when you were inspecting these buildings, did you talk to eye-witnesses; purported eye-witnesses, I must say?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: As far as I remember, you told us, yesterday, that you had forms prepared for each of the buildings?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: When you talked to the witnesses, did you write down their statements immediately into those forms?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Basically, in most cases, I just wrote a summary of what they said, along with their contact information, if available. But on the day that we -- at the time that we received the information, Mr. Herscher and I visited every site together. And we would usually have a division of labour. One of us would handle the camera; the other one would be recording information.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Riedlmayer, you will not hold it against me if I make a mistake, because I had to read a lot of documents. But I think I saw it, somewhere, that you ordered those interviews after you completed your day in Pristina. I mean, you ordered those notes about the talks you had with witnesses.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I simply organised the papers that we had from a single day's excursion. Because we were worried about mechanical malfunctions, or the possibility theft, we did not take computers along with us. So every day, when we set out into the field, we would take a large stack of photocopies of all the information we had about the sites we were going to visit that day. We also had a of blank forms to fill out for each site that we visited. When we would return in the evening, among the tasks would be sorting through these documents, making sure that we had records of which negative numbers referred to which sites, that kind of thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So in the course of a day, you would talk to certain persons. And then in the evening, when you organised your papers, you would write down the gist of those conversations. Is that a correct understanding?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The conversations were written down at the time that the conversations took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: But since you took notes, immediately, as you were talking, would you read back your notes to the person who gave you that information? And would the person authorise your notes by signing what you had written?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I told the Court, we were not in the business of taking depositions. We were simply taking basic information, and it was up to the Court, I believe, to see what -- whether to pursue that, in terms of subpoenaing witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your report, when discussing the objectives and methodology of your research, you said that you did not restrict yourself to monuments designated by the Institute for Culture as protected monuments. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Why did you not restrict yourself to those buildings designated as historic monuments by the Institute for the Cultural Heritage Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe, I set out the reasons in my expert report, but I can also sum it up now. First of all, because we -- our task, as we set it for ourselves, was to investigate all allegations made with respect to destruction of heritage. And many of those allegations involved sites that had not been granted legally protected status. Secondly, also because the list of protected monuments, in fact, had altered a number of times. And we were not sure really which of those to regard as authoritative. And, most importantly perhaps, because the distribution of sites, among the protected monuments was very uneven. There were many more protected sites that were Orthodox monuments than Islamic monuments. Only a little more than a dozen Islamic monuments, in all of Kosovo, had been designated as legally protected sites, whereas over 210 Orthodox sites had been.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I'm trying to find it in the record, but I got back in the interpretation that you said, "a dozen Islamic monuments." Is that a misinterpretation or is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe the total number was 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Riedlmayer, you said the reason for that was ideological and political. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Riedlmayer, are you aware that in 1977, at the time of Kosovo's full autonomy, even when the Institute for the Protection of Monuments of Kosovo was staffed mainly by Albanians, a law was passed on the protection of cultural monuments that designated a list of all protected cultural heritage?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you also know that this law was valid all the way until 1994?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not aware of when the law was changed. I do know that in the most recent pre-war document that we examined, that publication by the Institute for the Protection of Monuments, there were a number of designations of buildings that dated from the 1990s and which, I assume, could not have been included on the 1977 list.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Are you also aware that, by virtue of an UNMIK decree from December 1999, a decision was made on the laws to be applied in Kosovo, and that it was accepted to apply the law on the protection of the culture of Kosovo from 1977? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was aware of the UNMIK decree. I am also aware of subsequent UNMIK decrees that are now -- although I don't know whether they have been enacted into legislation yet, which, in order to avoid any contentious issue, simply designate all religious structures as protected monuments.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Since we agreed that this UNMIK decree from December 1999 restored this law from 1977, is it the case that, in the meantime, some new cultural property was included in the list of protected cultural property in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I understand your question. Could you repeat it, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: The gist of my question is this: You said that you doubt that this list of protected cultural monuments is completely free of ideological and political considerations, but what I want to know is, since UNMIK came to Kosovo and issued this decree to apply the law from 1977, is it the case that some new monuments found their way into that list?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the situation at present in Kosovo; however, with regard to this whole issue of designations, let me point out that, while there are certain objective criteria that can be used to designate sites for legal protection, such as age or prominence in the world literature, by and large, in addition to factors such as age, the main judgement is a value judgement as to what you consider to be important for a country, important for a government, to protect. And these are always issues that involve subjective considerations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just a moment. If you don't mind, Mr. Bakrac. I understood the question to be: Was it possible that the list, when reinstated in December 1999, might have been different in content from the list of 1977 because certain buildings had been added to it? Do you know the answer to that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Riedlmayer, are you aware that the UNESCO expert mission visited Kosovo after the war and the hostilities --

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes,

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: -- in 2004 and earlier? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: 2004 is after the conclusion of my study. I have read news reports of that; I have not seen what reports they have issued.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that you have not seen what reports they have issued, but do you happen to know whether they had anything to say about the list of cultural property prescribed by the law on the protection of cultural property of 1977?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you aware, sir - and, as a member of the Orthodox church, I don't wish to glorify it; I only want to deal in facts - but are you aware that the UNESCO mission which was in Kosovo from the 12th of March to the 18th of March, 2004, drew up a report which designated six cultural properties of the Orthodox heritage as the most significant, including Decani, Gracanica, Banjska, Sveti Archangel Mihail, Prizren, and the Church of Our Lady --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It may be that this is going to turn into something relevant, Mr. Bakrac, but what is the relevance of this particular question?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, well, that's why I prefaced my question by saying I didn't want to glorify one culture at the expense of others. I'm dealing with facts. The witness, in his expert report, seems to imply that the list of monuments was politically and ideologically coloured, and his only arguments are based on statistics, the proportion of Orthodox sites on the list compared to Islamic sites. I want to draw a parallel with the findings of an independent UNESCO commission and what it established after the war in Kosovo, whether they established any kind of evident discrepancy with respect to what Mr. Riedlmayer has been saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But do the findings of the body you're now referring to come to the conclusion that roughly 15 Islamic sites was a reasonable proportion to assign protection to in 1999? Which was the law, as I understand it, at the relevant period of this indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm only trying to establish whether there is a foundation for what Mr. Riedlmayer is saying, that these monuments were neglected for political and ideological reasons. If this was so, an independent UNESCO commission, I assume, would have had to correct such an irregularity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, it appears that they were looking at a situation where the 1977 list had been restored. They weren't comparing the situation in 1999, at the period of the indictment. Or have I misunderstood you?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, what I want to find out is whether the law of 1977, or rather, whether the witness knows of any cultural monument not in the list of 1977 but subsequently included based on the UNESCO findings. That's what I would like to find out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And how is that relevant to the case?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it's relevant to assess the objectiveness. All my questions refer to whether the expert report of Witness Riedlmayer is compromised in its objectivity by the facts. One fact is that his main field of research has been Islamic culture. I won't repeat all my questions from the beginning --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I don't dispute that you followed a line which is clearly comprehensible, and I was confining my question to you to the particular issue you're raising here. Now, it's impossible for us to judge whether this is, in fact, relevant; it doesn't look it. But, on the basis of your assurance that it will prove relevant, then -- sorry, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I didn't mean to interrupt, but before you finish, I had a different objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Which is?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: It has more to do with foundation. I can understand the line that -- I understand him to be pursuing, but without some more information about what this UNESCO report is and what its standards are and what it's based on, I don't know how we can begin to make any comparison that would shed light on whether or not Mr. Riedlmayer's opinion or position was objective.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, it may be that the foundation can be established through questioning Mr. Riedlmayer. Of course, if he has insufficient knowledge of these findings to give meaningful answers, then your objection would be well founded, Mr. Hannis. I will allow you to continue this, Mr. Bakrac, but we will be paying close attention to its relevance, bearing in mind that you're the one that's told us that the 1977 law was revoked in 1994, which seems, to me, to be the most relevant feature of this evidence so far.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I was trying to save time. As Mr. Riedlmayer did not deny this, I will refer to PD13, the UNMIK decree, which is in e-court, 5D14, "Decision, World Heritage Committee, 30 com 8(b)" -- [In English] 53 [Interpretation] and 5D15, the same decision, B54. We can look at these in e-court, and these are the documents on which my questions on the UNMIK decree and the UNESCO report were founded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Your first reference there was to something called PD13. What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: 5D13.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's 5D13. In any event, I think you should continue to seek an answer to the first question you asked. And if that can't be adequately answered by Mr. Riedlmayer, it may be necessary for you to go into these exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Riedlmayer, are you aware that, pursuant to the decisions I have read out and the inspection carried out by UNESCO in Kosovo, these six monuments, which were Orthodox monuments, were put on the World Heritage List?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I understand, only the Decani monastery was declared a World Heritage Site.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: That was in 2004. And in July 2006, all the other monasteries I've mentioned were added to Decani. Are you aware of this?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not of the latter, but in any event --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Allow the witness to finish the answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In any event, I wanted to say that all six of these were on the protected list to begin with, but that's six out of 210.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I'm referring to those monuments placed on the World Heritage List --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, now it's clear that you're asking about something I didn't understand you were asking about, in the first instance. I thought you were asking, earlier, about the list that related to Kosovo, that's the internal list of Serbia and Montenegro. And it seems to me, Mr. Bakrac, that the placing of these sites on the World Heritage List is immaterial; in 2004 and 2006, is immaterial to this indictment. So you should not pursue that line any further. Move on to something relevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will move on, Your Honours. My last question, however, is whether Mr. Riedlmayer knows whether the UNESCO commission, in respect of the list drawn up by Yugoslavia, or, rather, the 1977 law had any monuments to add to that list.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether anyone had anything to add to it, whether UNESCO did? I told you I have not read their report.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Riedlmayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I will now move on to the sites listed in the indictment. I hope we will move through this quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: In your report, Mr. Riedlmayer, and also in the course of your examination-in-chief, you said that you visited the Catholic church of St. Anthony in Djakovica.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: As far as I was able to understand, the site of that church was in the immediate vicinity of the JNA barracks. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: When you inspected the church, you established that only the glass had been shattered, as a result of the NATO bombing of the JNA barracks. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: When you inspected the church on site, did you notice any other damage? And had the glass already been replaced?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I noticed no other damage, and the glass had been fixed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You said that you received information that, immediately before the beginning of the bombing, the command and operative base of the Yugoslav army was there; that's what your report states.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's what the parish priest told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Are you aware that there was no command and no operations base there, but, rather, the medical platoon and that surgery was carried out there, with the previous approval of the Catholic priests. Are you aware of those facts?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not what the parish priest told me. I spoke to him in person, without an interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we have on e-court Exhibit 5D11. As the witness is an English speaker, but, as I understand it, he also reads Serbian; however, I would like to have it in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Riedlmayer, this is the order issued by the commander of the 52nd Artillery Rocket Brigade, Anti-Aircraft Defence, of the 19th of May, 1999, but the relocation of the medical platoon from the Catholic monastery --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I see it only talks about being relocated from the present location, without an indication as to what the present location is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in point 3, it says: "On relocation, hand over the Catholic monastery back in the same state that it was found when it was requisitioned." And it says: "A report is to be made and control damages to be established. The building is to be restored to the same condition it was found before moving in."

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So are you aware that an unarmed medical platoon, which only dealt with wounded, was located there with the approval of the Catholic priests?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I only know what the Catholic parish priest told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And you said that the Catholic priest told you that there were signs of vandalism. Did he describe these signs?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He told me that computers, televisions, and other equipment had been looted from the building, and that the walls had been defaced, and that, in short, the place was not inhabitable when they came back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think your report said that that was for a period of two months?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And that's from the beginning of the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Which is fairly consistent of moving out on the 19th of May?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. He told me he -- the priest told me he stayed in Djakovica throughout the war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: This particular order is dated the 19th of May, as you'll see.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And he told you that somebody had scraped the walls on purpose, and these were the traces of vandalism. Is that what you wanted --

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't say scraped the walls; he said defaced, whatever that may mean. We were speaking in Turkish. He came from Prizren and he knows Turkish. And I lived in Turkey for three years, so I can speak Turkish.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I understand that. But he didn't tell you anything about the kind of damage; he just said that it was necessary for the walls to be whitewashed. But he didn't say what kind of damage this was.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He said the doors and windows were broken and that the furnishings, including computers and other equipment, had been taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Very well. We understand that, the doors and the windows, as a result of the NATO bombing and -- of course, I'm not trying to justify theft. If it's true that the computers and other equipment were stolen, I don't justify it. But it doesn't amount to destruction of cultural property; it's common theft. But let's move on to another site, Mr. Riedlmayer. The stari bazaar in Pec, the old market. Did you, yourself, visit that site?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I have before me part of your finding, where it says that the photograph was taken by Begolli and the other photograph was taken by Xhavit Lokaj, and it doesn't say anything under who inspected the site. There's no record of the fact that you conducted the inspection, in your notes.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I specified that in my statement in court yesterday, that it was I who inspected the site. As for the photographs, the pre-war photograph from Mr. Begolli I solicited myself. Mr. Begolli runs a photographic shop in town, and I was told that he had recent pre-war photographs. So I approached him and he went through his negatives and came up with several of them. I chose this one because it happens to match the shot taken by Mr. Lokaj. Now, Mr. Lokaj was there just a month after the end of the war, and I put his photograph in the database because it shows a clear picture of what it looked like immediately after the war. When I was there, some of the shops already were beginning to get fixed up. You could still see the damage quite clearly, but it wasn't as clean a documentation as you would have, you know, immediately in the aftermath of the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, what's the exhibit number for that one?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is part of P1550.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Riedlmayer, you furthermore did not designate any of the persons you interviewed or who supplied you with information. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where? In this particular record?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes. The old bazaar in Pec. I have your report before me in English. It says "Information Statements" and it's blank. And where it says "Media Reports," it's also blank.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So there was no information, no media reports, but this did not prevent you from assessing the damage to the report, or rather, from saying that it was burnt down by the Serb police in June 1999. Why did you note this where you should have described the nature of the damage, which was your task?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. In this case, I didn't have a single person who came up and, sort of, formally informed me. I spoke to several residents who barraged me with information. I should have, I assume, kept the information to the description itself, given that I could see that. The damage was quite clear in terms of seeing marks of burning; also, bulldozer tracks where the rubble had been pushed to the backs of sites. What --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Riedlmayer --

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't think he was finished answering the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Excuse me, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: So when people told me that these shops had been burned and then bulldozed, it seemed like a reasonable remark. As to the time when this happened, I just wrote down what people told me at the time. I should have noted the name of an informant; I regret I did not in this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Riedlmayer, you have just told us that you noted on the spot what people told you. Isn't that what you said just a little while ago, that you noted down everything people told you immediately? Now we see that, in fact, you did not.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean? What I have on my entry in the database is what I copied from my handwritten form. The handwritten form consists of the notes I took in the field. You know, I was out in the field and I took very short -- brief notes, in many instances, since we had a lot of field to cover.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I am waiting for the interpretation. I also had the impression that Your Honour wished to say something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, I've changed my mind, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Riedlmayer, it's almost time for a break. Are you trying to tell me that you have the names and details of the persons you talked to but did not include them in the form?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. What I'm trying to tell you is that in this case I neglected to take names.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And on site you saw evidence that the Serb police burnt down the bazaar in June. Is that what you were trying to say?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Don't answer that question, Mr. Riedlmayer. If you are putting a serious point, Mr. Bakrac, then put it in a serious way.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I see it's time for a break, and I will move on to a different site after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, there is no reason why you can't ask the source of that information, but I think we made it clear yesterday that, where a statement of that nature depended on a general proposition coming from, for example, the organisations that Mr. Riedlmayer spoke to who said this was the information they had or, if it's come from, as he describes it here, a barrage of information from people, then we would never draw a conclusion that that accurately reflected who carried out this attack or, indeed, that that what necessarily happened on the occasion. He's already acknowledged the weakness of that material. Mr. Hannis has indicated a number of times yesterday that what actually happened depends on information from other sources. The principal evidence we're getting from Mr. Riedlmayer is the nature of the damage. But also where there is some specific indication of the cause from his investigation or from what was said to him by someone he's identified, then he's reflected that and that's something that may have some weight, in due course. But I think it will be easy for you to identify the parts of that report to which we would give no weight in isolation and those that may carry some weight even on their own. So, we will be adjourning now, Mr. Riedlmayer, for 20 minutes or so. Could you again go with the usher, and we'll see you at ten minutes to 11.00. Just leave the courtroom. The practice we're following now is for the witness to leave before the Court does.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And we'll assume at ten to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Riedlmayer, before the break we discussed the Catholic convent and then we moved on to the bazaar in Pec, but I just missed out on one thing in my notes; namely, that in your report you also stated that the army of Yugoslavia used the Catholic church in Pristina; namely, to place an air defence radar on its tower. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what the parish priest told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I just want to know whether you pursued this interest any further. Do you know how the radar works, and its antenna system? It cannot be placed on a tower because it emits electrical and magnetic waves and cannot deal with obstacles. Doesn't that make the claim of this priest absolutely absurd and illogical? Plus another question which is a part of this: Can you estimate in how many seconds NATO would have located that radar and destroyed it?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to object. That's a compound question. I don't know which of the three he's supposed to answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Let's take them one question at a time, please, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So, first of all, you received this information from the Catholic priest. My first question is: Did you cross-check this allegation? Did you verify it in any way?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was there merely to verify what happened to the church during the war. The church seemed to be in good shape. I talked to the priest, who had spent the entire war in the rectory building right next to the church, and when I asked him what had happened to his church during the war, this is what he told me, so I wrote it down. I am, as I have already stated, not an expert on military installations and I had no way of verifying whether this was either technically feasible or whether it, in fact, happened. I took down the information and I took down the priest's contact information and therewith I saw my task in this regard to have been fulfilled.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So, if I understand you correctly - and it's necessary for the record - you do not know the weight of that radar or how it was hoisted on the top of the church cathedral.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, Mr. Riedlmayer is not here fighting a case. Mr. Riedlmayer had a job to do. He's explained both to Mr. Hannis and you what that job was, how he did it, and what the limitations were so far as this case is concerned. I don't think it's really fair to him to then go over details as if you're trying to make a point, when it's perfectly plain from his answer that he had no way of verifying the information that was given to him at all. And he is no military expert and he won't know the detail of radar installations or anything of that nature. Now, that's something you can found upon in due course when it comes to assessing the value of the report for our purposes, bearing in mind that he was doing it for a different purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I will move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit P1773 deals with a mosque in Orahovac, built in 1916, in modern times. Did you assess the mosque on the spot.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which is the mosque? I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Celine.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: In the village of Celine, Orahovac municipality.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You, personally, or Mr. Herscher made the assessment of that site.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not personally visit that village. This is one of the sites where we made our assessment based on photographs. I think in this case the assessment that the building was completely destroyed is not hard to conclude from the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And based on the photographs, you concluded that the mosque was burned down by Serbs and that the Serbs razed it to the ground using a bulldozer. That's what you concluded on the basis of photographs.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As I explained in the direct examination, that is the information that was provided for me by the Islamic community, which I note in the report. The visual evidence of what you see there is consistent with that. I noted the pile of rubble, the burnt timbers, and the intact houses in the background.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: But, Mr. Riedlmayer, wouldn't it have been enough to say that the mosque was burned down and completely destroyed? Wasn't that the mission of your research, to establish damage, rather than who inflicted the damage, from a third-hand source? In this case, you had no witnesses and no media reports.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We're becoming very impatient, Mr. Bakrac, with this. You know perfectly what the job was that Mr. Riedlmayer was doing, including noting any information that might be of use to establish the circumstances in which the damage was done. But he, by no means, meant to establish that on the basis of what he heard. He made it clear to you that he was hoping to give guidance to others who might find it useful to follow these leads up. And he's made it clear already in his evidence that what he was doing when he noted these circumstances, in the section you're referring to, that he was noting down what he had learned from information given by others.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Riedlmayer, you said information came from the Islamic community. What I see here is "International Management Group" as the source of this information. It was their database.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. If you go down to the bottom, you will see that Mr. Sabri Bajgora is also listed. He was the contact person at the Islamic community who provided me with the photos and some of the information.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Why isn't he mentioned in the line that says, "Citizen providing the information"? He's designated only as the photographer.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Down below it says, "Surveyor." "Surveyor" is shorthand for source of information. All the way at the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I see that. But there is also a line, "Citizen Reports," with the names of one or two citizens. You did not mention that Mr. Bajgora made one such report himself. I see him only in a different line, together with the International Management Group database.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Can we have a reference to what page we're on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think it's informants' statements in the English version that Mr. Bakrac is looking at.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I understood we were talking about the Celine mosque.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And there are no informant statements.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And so your question is, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: My question is: Did you receive information from the International Management Group?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not. I merely received their database, which consists entirely of photographs and technical descriptions of buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: From whom, then, did you receive information as to what had happened; that is, who did it?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This particular information came from Mr. Bajgora. The reason, in case that's what you were aiming at, that his name appears here, rather than as a separate informant statement, is because for convenience sake, since so many of my photographs of mosques came from the Islamic community, for brevity's sake, given that the information was usually very brief and often sketchy, I often incorporated it in the first page, rather than going on to the second page of the survey report.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Riedlmayer, now I would like to know about the mosque in Orahovac municipality, Bela Crkva. Did you personally, or Mr. Herscher, perform the assessment of that one yourselves? It's P1774.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Bela Crkva is not one of the sites that we visited personally; however, here we had photographs from multiple sources. We made our assessment on the photographs and information we had, rather than a firsthand site visit.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: As for information, I also see no informants named. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you would scroll down on the e-court display, please. Okay. We had --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: We can move one page further. You will see informants there.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I think it's this similar situation, as to what we had with Celine. We had the photographs, and we had some very minimal information from Mr. Bajgora. We, however, had photographs also from two other sources showing the same damage. And so we felt fairly confident in our damage assessment. It's a building we assessed as having been heavily damaged, and the minaret blown up.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: In this case you also had some media reports; whereas, yesterday, you said that you never took media reports without other corroborating information from witnesses or eye-witnesses. Did I understand that correctly?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe you did not understand it correctly. Our criteria were we never included a site in our report, based exclusively on media reports. Media reports were an add-on, if we had information from the sources we considered reliable, which are listed in our report. And there was also a media report which could help to pin-point the date or stage of the damage, we would include that. But we had no criteria saying we wouldn't include media reports unless we also had witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, if you look at the media reports, you will see that there are parts highlighted which Mr. Riedlmayer considered relevant. And each of the highlighted parts relates to the state of the mosque, and you have a date for the media report. And the state of the mosque, as described in these, is being said by Mr. Riedlmayer to be consistent with the photographs. And that's the only use to which he was putting these media reports, as he explained yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll move on to another site, P175, the mosque in Brestovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you agree that's another location that you never visited?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think that's P1775.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's what I said. Maybe it was a slip of the tongue.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So that's another location that you did not visit yourself. Is it also correct that you have no informant statements here or any media reports again?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Could you please scroll down, all the way. Okay. Here, we had photographs from two independent sources, and we made our conclusions on the basis of the photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Riedlmayer, you say you based it on photographs from the International Management Group database. Didn't you say in your report that that group dealt only with modern buildings?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say they dealt only with modern buildings. Their primary mission had to do with establishing the state of infrastructure in these municipalities. So they primarily dealt with public buildings of all sorts; however, as a public facility, they included what they called heritage facilities, which included houses of worship. Insofar as they were able to provide photographs taken in these places, their teams covered many more villages than we were able to visit ourselves, and so they provided that information in the photographs. In every case we made a good-faith effort to corroborate information from multiple sources.
